headline: This 2020 law lets servicemembers end a lease early without an early termination fee if they receive a stop movement order because of an emergency.
what_it_does: The law applies to service members who signed a lease after receiving certain military orders, such as a permanent change of station, a deployment, or individual support of military operations. If a stop movement order for at least 30 days or an indefinite period is later issued because of a local, national, or global emergency, the service member may terminate a lease for housing or a motor vehicle. No early termination fee may be charged. For a housing lease, the stop movement order must keep the service member or their dependents from living in the home.

who_it_affects.group: Active-duty servicemembers who sign housing or vehicle leases after receiving permanent change of station, deployment, or support orders
who_it_affects.how: They may end the lease early and avoid an early termination fee if an emergency stop movement order blocks their move.

who_it_affects.group: Dependents of servicemembers who live in leased housing
who_it_affects.how: For a housing lease, the stop movement order must prevent them from occupying the home for the law to apply.

who_it_affects.group: Landlords and vehicle lessors who rent to servicemembers
who_it_affects.how: They cannot collect an early termination fee when a covered servicemember ends a lease under this law.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted August 14, 2020; the official summary does not state a separate effective date.
